posts.title: envsafe v0.2 keeps .env secrets out of agent transcripts
posts.description: envsafe v0.2.0, a command-line tool and MCP server, lets AI agents and people edit .env files without secret values ever reaching chat, terminal output, or logs.
posts.html:
envsafe v0.2.0 is out. It edits .env files for AI coding agents and the people who work alongside them, and it never prints a secret value. Values go in through standard input, an environment variable, or a file. What comes back is key names, line numbers, and exit codes.

The problem it addresses is ordinary. An agent is asked to rotate an API token. To find the right line, it runs cat .env. Every credential in the file is now in the chat transcript, the terminal scrollback, and whatever log the session ships to. A quick sed edit can do the same thing in reverse: the new token ends up in the command line, and shell history keeps it. The agent did nothing malicious. It used the only tools it had.

envsafe swaps those tools for commands that cannot leak:

printf '%s' "$NEW_TOKEN" | envsafe set API_TOKEN --stdin --dry-run
envsafe list
envsafe validate --schema .env.example

The dry run shows what would change. Values appear as <redacted>, and each change is labeled would add or would update. set is an upsert by default. --only-existing refuses to create a key that is not there, which catches typos. --only-new refuses to overwrite one that is. list prints only key names, unless asked for masked markers. validate reports syntax errors, duplicate keys, and required keys that are missing or empty, checked against a .env.example or a Markdown/AsciiDoc variable registry. The set command accepts no value on the command line at all.

The files stay as their authors wrote them. Comments, blank lines, section headers, quoting, export prefixes, and CRLF line endings all survive an edit byte for byte. Writes are atomic, and the tool never adds a byte-order mark. New in v0.2.0, the comment lines directly above a key now belong to that key. set --comment adds or replaces them. unset leaves them in place unless --with-comment is passed. New keys can go after a named key (--after) or at the end of a section (--section "# == Mail =="). envsafe refuses any comment that contains the value being set.

Also new in v0.2.0: envsafe mcp runs a Model Context Protocol server over stdio. It exposes envsafe_set, envsafe_unset, envsafe_list, and envsafe_validate. The set tool takes no inline value argument, because tool arguments pass through the model’s context. It reads the value from an environment variable the server can see, or from a file.

Install

Windows users can install the MSI from the v0.2.0 release, which puts envsafe on PATH. The same release has archives for Linux x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64, plus SHA-256 checksums.

To register the MCP server in Cursor (.cursor/mcp.json):

{ "mcpServers": { "envsafe": { "command": "envsafe", "args": ["mcp"] } } }

In Claude Code:

claude mcp add envsafe -- envsafe mcp

Other MCP clients use the same stdio command, envsafe mcp.

envsafe is written in D, is MIT-licensed, and also ships as a library. Source, documentation, and the issue tracker are at github.com/dev-centr/envsafe. A move command and Windows arm64 builds are not in this release.

posts.title: A Control Panel for all Config file types
posts.description: UniConfig Config Panel opens INI, YAML, TOML, SDLang, and tfvars with schema-backed settings widgets — including fields the file never mentioned.
posts.html:
UniConfig’s Config Panel opens other people’s INI, YAML, TOML, SDLang, and tfvars with schema-backed settings widgets.

Fields the file never mentioned still appear when the schema knows them — a Control Panel posture for config, not a raw text dump.

posts.html:
New additions landed in the Business Bootstrap guide on docs.devcentr.org.

Scheduling, design, and vault capability areas expand the same support-systems guide — growth in place, not a second parallel handbook.

posts.title: MSI-generator v0.2 released
posts.description: msi-generator v0.2 writes real OLE2 compound files, cabinets, and core Windows Installer tables — still unsigned, no longer an empty stub.
posts.html:
MSI-generator v0.2 is released.

The tool now writes real OLE2 compound files, cabinets, and core Windows Installer tables. Builds are still unsigned; the empty stub era is over.

posts.title: DevCentr’s new install tool, Ibex, released
posts.description: Ibex (Install Builder EXtension): CLI and Explorer actions for installer projects, in-place PATH installs, and CI pipeline emit.
posts.html:
DevCentr’s new install tool, Ibex, is released.

Ibex (Install Builder EXtension) covers CLI and Explorer actions for installer projects, in-place PATH installs, and CI pipeline emit — a host for installer work rather than one more one-off script.

posts.title: Partnership with OpenShellOrg
posts.description: DevCentr and OpenShellOrg lock the sibling story: toolchain ownership here, shell entrypoint honesty there.
posts.html:
DevCentr and OpenShellOrg formalized a sibling partnership: toolchain ownership on the DevCentr side, shell entrypoint honesty on theirs.

The split keeps install and development tools from pretending to be the user’s shell — and keeps the shell from pretending to own the toolchain.

Figure 1. Sibling ownership

Links worth bookmarking: OpenShellOrg, their docs, Toolchain Management Pattern, and the alignment page in general-knowledge (Dev-Centr and OpenShellOrg).

posts.title: News desk opens
posts.description: DevCentr opens a public News feed for shipped work and partnerships — not a dump of every docs edit.
posts.html:
DevCentr now publishes a public News desk for work that entered the shared record: releases, partnerships, and durable openings.

Day-to-day shipping notes stay on the Changelog. Essays and unfinished directions live on the Blog.

posts.title: Help hub opens beside the docs
posts.description: A Help hub lands so "I need assistance" no longer means "go read the manual."
posts.html:
DevCentr opened a Help hub beside the documentation so people who need assistance get a path that is not "start at page one of the manual."

The hub routes common asks — account, install, breakage — without pretending every answer belongs in a reference page.

posts.title: Brand mark stays in open SVG
posts.description: The DevCentr mark ships as open SVG motion — not a proprietary player dependency for an open brand.
posts.html:
The DevCentr brand mark stays in open SVG, including motion that does not require a proprietary player.

That choice keeps an open-source org’s identity readable in ordinary browsers and docs — without baking a closed runtime into the logo.
